gapFill.title: Fill in the gaps
gapFill.subtitle: Type the past simple form. Twenty original sentences — completed actions, sequences, past habits, negatives and questions. Every sentence has a finished-time marker.

questions.explain: A finished action at a specific past time: last Saturday.
‘Yesterday morning’ — a clear, finished time in the past.
‘Buy’ is irregular: buy → bought.

questions.after: my umbrella on the train yesterday.
questions.explain: ‘Leave’ is irregular: leave → left.

questions.after: the meeting at the last minute last Friday.
questions.explain: ‘Cancel’ doubles its l in British English (cancelled); American English writes canceled.
One completed action after another: the film finished, then we walked home.

questions.before: He finished his homework, and then he
questions.explain: ‘Then’ links two completed actions, one after the other.
‘Get’ is irregular: get → got.

questions.before: When I was a child, I
questions.after: a bike to school every day.
questions.explain: A repeated habit that’s now over — past simple, not present.

questions.after: football every weekend when we were kids.
questions.explain: ‘Every weekend’ describes a past routine, now finished.
A hobby she had when she was young — a past habit, now finished.

questions.after: in this town his whole life, until he died in 2010.
questions.explain: A finished past state: he lived here until his death, so use past simple.

questions.before: When I was a teenager, I
questions.after: hard for every test at school.
questions.explain: A past habit at a finished time (‘when I was a teenager’). Consonant + y → change y to i before -ed: studied.
Negative past simple: didn’t + base verb.
After ‘didn’t’, the verb goes back to its base form: go, not went.
‘Didn’t’ + base verb — never ‘didn’t finished’.

questions.after: the bus on Monday, so we walked.
questions.explain: Negative past simple with the base form: catch, not caught.
Past simple questions start with did + subject + base verb: Did you call…?
‘The tickets’ is plural, and questions with be don’t use ‘did’: Were the tickets…?
Past simple questions start with did + subject + base verb: Did he pass…?

wordOrder.title: Put it in order
wordOrder.subtitle: Tap the words to build each sentence — 20 examples covering completed actions, sequences, past habits, negatives, and questions.

matching.title: Match the past forms
matching.subtitle: Tap a base verb, then tap its irregular past simple form. These twenty don’t take -ed — they’re the ones learners mix up most.

timedMC.title: Beat the clock
timedMC.subtitle: 15 seconds per question. Check the time marker (yesterday, last year, ago) and watch the irregular verbs and the -ed spellings.

questions.text: I        to Rome last year.
wrongReasons: Wrong tense: ‘last year’ is finished, so the present ‘go’ doesn’t fit.
Wrong tense: the present perfect can’t go with a finished time like ‘last year’.
Wrong tense: ‘am going’ is present continuous, but the trip is over.
questions.explain: ‘Last year’ is a finished time — past simple. ‘Go’ is irregular: went.

questions.text: She        her arm skiing last winter.
wrongReasons: Wrong tense: ‘last winter’ is finished, so not the present ‘breaks’.
Wrong tense: the present perfect can’t go with ‘last winter’.
‘Break’ is irregular — the past is ‘broke’, not ‘breaked’.
questions.explain: ‘Break’ is irregular: break → broke.

questions.text: We        dinner together two days ago.
wrongReasons: Wrong tense: ‘two days ago’ is past, but ‘have’ is present.
Wrong tense: the present perfect can’t go with ‘ago’.
‘Have’ is irregular — the past is ‘had’, not ‘haved’.
questions.explain: ‘Ago’ marks a finished time — past simple ‘had’.

questions.text: The train        ten minutes late yesterday.
wrongReasons: Wrong tense: ‘yesterday’ is finished, so not the present ‘arrives’.
Wrong tense: the present perfect can’t go with ‘yesterday’.
Wrong tense: ‘will arrive’ is future, but ‘yesterday’ is past.
questions.explain: ‘Yesterday’ is a finished time — past simple ‘arrived’.

questions.text: They        their house in 2019.
wrongReasons: Wrong tense: ‘2019’ is finished, so not the present ‘sell’.
Wrong tense: the present perfect can’t go with a year like ‘2019’.
Wrong tense: ‘are selling’ is present continuous, but 2019 is over.
questions.explain: ‘In 2019’ is a finished time — past simple. ‘Sell’ is irregular: sold.

questions.text: She came home,        a shower and went to bed.
wrongReasons: Wrong tense: ‘came’ and ‘went’ are past, so ‘has’ (present) doesn’t fit.
Wrong tense: ‘have’ is present; the whole sequence is in the past.
Wrong tense: the present perfect doesn’t fit a finished sequence of events.
questions.explain: Events in a finished sequence all take the past simple: came, had, went.

questions.text: He opened the letter and        the news at once.
wrongReasons: Wrong tense: ‘opened’ is past, so ‘reads’ (present) doesn’t fit.
Wrong tense: the present perfect doesn’t fit a finished sequence.
‘Read’ is irregular — the past is ‘read’ (said /red/), not ‘readed’.
questions.explain: ‘Read’ is irregular: the spelling doesn’t change, but the past is said /red/.

questions.text: First we paid, then we        the restaurant.
wrongReasons: Wrong tense: ‘paid’ is past, so ‘leave’ (present) doesn’t fit.
‘Leave’ is irregular — the past is ‘left’, not ‘leaved’.
Wrong tense: the present perfect doesn’t fit a finished sequence.
questions.explain: ‘First we paid, then we…’ is a past sequence — past simple. ‘Leave’ is irregular: left.

questions.text: As a teenager, I        in the sea every morning.
wrongReasons: Wrong tense: ‘as a teenager’ is finished, so not the present ‘swim’.
‘Swim’ is irregular — the past is ‘swam’, not ‘swimmed’.
Wrong tense: the present perfect can’t go with ‘as a teenager’.
questions.explain: A habit in a finished period — past simple. ‘Swim’ is irregular: swam.

questions.text: My grandparents        in a small village in the 1970s.
wrongReasons: Wrong tense: ‘in the 1970s’ is finished, so not the present ‘grow up’.
‘Grow’ is irregular — the past is ‘grew’, not ‘growed’.
Wrong tense: the present perfect can’t go with ‘in the 1970s’.
questions.explain: A finished period — past simple. ‘Grow’ is irregular: grew.

questions.text: She        the piano for years before she stopped.
wrongReasons: Wrong tense: ‘before she stopped’ shows the habit is over, so not the present ‘practises’.
Wrong form: with ‘she’ a present verb needs -s, and the sentence is past anyway.
Wrong tense: the present perfect suggests she still plays — but she stopped.
questions.explain: A finished past habit — past simple ‘practised’.

questions.text: I        the news at all yesterday.
wrongReasons: After ‘didn’t’ the verb goes back to its base form: ‘hear’, not ‘heard’.
Wrong tense: ‘yesterday’ is finished, so not the present ‘don’t hear’.
Wrong tense: the present perfect can’t go with ‘yesterday’.
questions.explain: Negatives use didn’t + base verb: didn’t hear.

questions.text: They        the deadline last week.
wrongReasons: Wrong tense: ‘last week’ is finished, so not the present ‘don’t meet’.
Wrong tense: the present perfect can’t go with ‘last week’.
After ‘didn’t’ the verb goes back to its base form: ‘meet’, not ‘met’.
questions.explain: Negatives use didn’t + base verb: didn’t meet.

questions.text: We        enough time to finish the test yesterday.
wrongReasons: After ‘didn’t’ the verb goes back to its base form: ‘have’, not ‘had’.
Wrong tense: ‘yesterday’ is finished, so not the present ‘don’t have’.
Wrong tense: the present perfect can’t go with ‘yesterday’.
questions.explain: Negatives use didn’t + base verb: didn’t have.

questions.text: the concert last night?
wrongReasons: Wrong tense: ‘last night’ is finished, so not the present ‘Do you enjoy’.
Wrong tense: the present perfect can’t go with ‘last night’.
Wrong tense: ‘Are you enjoying’ is present continuous, but the concert is over.
questions.explain: Past questions use Did + subject + base verb.

questions.text: Why        the office so late yesterday?
wrongReasons: Wrong tense: ‘yesterday’ is finished, so not the present ‘does she leave’.
Wrong tense: the present perfect can’t go with ‘yesterday’.
Wrong tense: ‘will she leave’ is future, but ‘yesterday’ is past.
questions.explain: Past questions use Did + subject + base verb, also after a question word.

questions.text: the hotel easily when they arrived?
wrongReasons: Wrong tense: ‘when they arrived’ is past, so not the present ‘Do they find’.
Wrong tense: the present perfect doesn’t fit a finished past moment.
Wrong tense: ‘Are they finding’ is present continuous, but the moment is past.
questions.explain: Past questions use Did + subject + base verb.

questions.text: Last summer we        the whole trip in advance.
wrongReasons: Spelling: a short verb ending in vowel + consonant doubles the consonant — planned.
Wrong tense: ‘last summer’ is finished, so not the present ‘plan’.
Wrong tense: the present perfect can’t go with ‘last summer’.
questions.explain: Short verb (consonant–vowel–consonant): double the consonant — plan → planned.

questions.text: The baby        all night last night.
wrongReasons: Wrong tense: ‘last night’ is finished, so not the present ‘cries’.
Wrong tense: ‘last night’ needs the past, but ‘cry’ is the present base form.
Wrong tense: the present perfect can’t go with ‘last night’.
questions.explain: Consonant + y becomes -ied: cry → cried.

questions.text: Yesterday he        to fix the bike himself.
wrongReasons: Spelling: consonant + y becomes -ied — tried, not ‘tryed’.
Wrong tense: ‘yesterday’ is finished, so not the present ‘tries’.
Wrong tense: the present perfect can’t go with ‘yesterday’.
questions.explain: Consonant + y becomes -ied: try → tried.

errorCorrection.title: Find the mistake
errorCorrection.subtitle: Each sentence has exactly one mistake. Tap the word you think is wrong. Twenty original sentences.

items.message: ‘Go’ is irregular: go → went, not ‘goed’.
‘Buy’ is irregular: buy → bought, not ‘buyed’.
‘Eat’ is irregular: eat → ate, not ‘eated’.
‘Think’ is irregular: think → thought, not ‘thinked’.
‘Bring’ is irregular: bring → brought, not ‘bringed’.
Short verb (consonant–vowel–consonant): double the consonant — dropped.
Consonant + y becomes -ied: copy → copied.
Short verb (consonant–vowel–consonant): double the consonant — chatted.
Consonant + y becomes -ied: try → tried.
With ‘we’ the past of ‘be’ is ‘were’, not ‘was’.
‘Yesterday’ is a finished time — ‘walked’, not ‘walks’.
‘Last night’ is a finished time — ‘cooked’, not ‘cook’.
‘In 2015’ is a finished time — ‘moved’, not ‘move’.
‘Ago’ marks a finished time — ‘called’, not ‘calls’.
‘Last summer’ is a finished time — ‘visited’, not ‘visit’.
‘Didn’t’ is already correct — the verb after it goes back to its base form: ‘go’, not ‘went’.
‘Didn’t’ is already correct — the verb after it goes back to its base form: ‘see’, not ‘saw’.
‘Did’ is already correct — the verb after it goes back to its base form: ‘go’, not ‘went’.
‘Last week’ is finished — the negative is ‘didn’t’, not ‘doesn’t’.
‘Yesterday’ is finished — the negative is ‘didn’t’, not ‘doesn’t’.

levelCheck.title: How well do you know it?
levelCheck.subtitle: 20 mixed questions — typing, word order, irregular forms, multiple choice, and spot-the-mistake. One pass, then a breakdown of where you’re strong and where to go back and practise.

items.sentText: I {{blank}} a cake for her birthday last week.
items.explain: A finished action at a specific past time: last week.

items.sentText: She {{blank}} her passport, so she couldn’t get on the plane.
items.explain: Negative past simple: didn’t + base verb — bring, not brought.

items.sentText: Years ago, my grandmother {{blank}} a little shop near the station.
items.explain: A past state, now finished — past simple.
Past simple questions start with did + subject + base verb: Did you buy…?

wrongReasons: There’s no such form as "haved" — "have" is irregular: have → had.
This is the present form, but ‘yesterday’ is past.
This is the present form, and ‘has’ doesn’t go with ‘I’.
items.explain: ‘Have’ is irregular: the past simple is ‘had’, for every subject.

items.text: In yesterday’s match, he {{blank}} the ball straight into the net.
wrongReasons: This is present simple, but ‘yesterday’ is past.
There’s no such form as "shooted" — "shoot" is irregular: shoot → shot.
The present perfect can’t go with ‘yesterday’s match’.

items.text: They {{blank}} us the truth last week.
wrongReasons: There’s no such form as "telled" — "tell" is irregular: tell → told.
This is present simple, but the sentence is about the past.
‘Has’ doesn’t go with ‘they’, and the present perfect doesn’t fit a finished story.

items.text: Yesterday I {{blank}} my glasses on the bus.
wrongReasons: This is the base form, not the past.
There’s no such form as "leaved" — "leave" is irregular: leave → left.
‘Has’ doesn’t go with ‘I’.
Wrong tense: ‘last Saturday’ is finished, so not the present ‘Do they win’.
Wrong tense: the present perfect can’t go with ‘last Saturday’.
Wrong tense: ‘Were they winning’ is past continuous — it asks about an action in progress, not the result.
items.explain: Past simple questions start with ‘did’ + subject + base verb.

items.text: We {{blank}} the whole cake last night.
wrongReasons: Wrong tense: ‘last night’ is finished, so not the present ‘eat’.
Wrong tense: the present perfect can’t go with ‘last night’.
Wrong tense: ‘will eat’ is future, but ‘last night’ is past.

items.text: He {{blank}} the email before yesterday’s deadline.
wrongReasons: Wrong tense: ‘yesterday’ is finished, so not the present ‘doesn’t send’.
After ‘didn’t’ the verb goes back to its base form: ‘send’, not ‘sent’.
The present perfect can’t go with ‘yesterday’s deadline’.
items.explain: Negatives use didn’t + base verb: didn’t send.

items.text: When she was little, she {{blank}} scared of the dark.
wrongReasons: Wrong tense: ‘when she was little’ is past, so not the present ‘is’.
Wrong tense: the present perfect suggests she’s still scared now.
‘Were’ doesn’t agree with ‘she’.
items.explain: The past of ‘be’ is ‘was’ for I/he/she/it and ‘were’ for you/we/they.

items.message: "Run" is irregular: run → ran, not runned.
Consonant + y becomes -ied: hurry → hurried.
After "didn’t", the verb goes back to its base form — "buy", not "bought".
"Last week" is a finished time — this needs past simple, not present simple.
